title: The Painted Ledger
premise: Ivo Villalobos, the cathedral's reclusive archivist, receives a letter confessing to a decades-old murder in the locked crypt—signed with their own childhood name—and a second letter promising a new death every week the ledger stays sealed. As Ivo decodes the painted ledger hidden beneath the cathedral's restored frescoes, they uncover a ring of city fathers who bought their survival during the war by selling neighbors' names, and realize the confessor is someone they trusted. In the end, Ivo must choose between turning the evidence over before the statute expires and protecting the one person who ever saw them clearly; they choose truth, sealing the crypt's last secret with their own confession.
about_author: Marguerite Nakamura is a former conservator of ecclesiastical archives who spent twelve years restoring illuminated manuscripts across Iberia and Japan. She writes mysteries from a converted bell tower, where she claims the drafts are always cold and the ink always honest.

chapters.title: Twin Envelopes
chapters.summary: Ivo Villalobos, cataloguing the cathedral's restricted holdings, opens two letters delivered the same hour: one confessing to a murder in the locked crypt forty years ago, signed 'Ivo,' and one promising weekly deaths until the painted ledger is found. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the vertigo of being addressed at all after a lifetime of deliberate invisibility.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Ivo inspects the crypt, finding the seal intact but a fresh scratch on the inner door—a door that only opens from inside. They photograph everything but tell no one, including Father Anselm. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into curiosity; the archivist's instinct to document outruns the instinct to flee.

chapters.title: A Death on Schedule
chapters.summary: A retired verger is found dead in his garden, an hour after the second letter promised. Police call it a heart attack; Ivo recognizes the timing as a message meant for them alone. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: guilt—the first price of staying silent arrives immediately.

chapters.title: Inspector Reyes
chapters.summary: Inspector Reyes, sharp and unfooled, interviews Ivo about the verger and notices Ivo flinched at the word 'crypt.' Their sparring establishes an uneasy alliance of mutual suspicion. POV: Ivo, with a brief Reyes interlude. Emotional beat: the terror of being seen by someone trained to look.

chapters.title: What the Frescoes Hide
chapters.summary: Restoration scaffolding reveals pigment anomalies in the nave frescoes; Ivo maps them against the cathedral's oldest inventory and finds entries for a ledger that no longer exists in any index. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into fear—the archive is starting to answer back.

chapters.title: The Name I Abandoned
chapters.summary: The confessor's letters use Ivo's birth name, known only to those from the village of San Remei. Flashbacks reveal Ivo's wartime childhood: the night families vanished, the night Ivo survived by saying nothing. POV: Ivo (past and present). Emotional beat: grief for the child who learned invisibility as armor.

chapters.title: Father Anselm's Silence
chapters.summary: Ivo confronts Anselm about the crypt's history; the old priest admits the diocese sealed it in 1963 and burned its records, then begs Ivo to let the dead stay dead. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: betrayal—loyalty to the church that sheltered Ivo now looks like complicity.

chapters.title: Second Week
chapters.summary: A city notary dies, again on schedule, again plausibly natural. Ivo finds a slip of ledger paper in their own desk drawer: a column of names, two struck through. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the horror of realizing the killer can enter the archive at will—or already lives there.

chapters.title: Decoding the Paint
chapters.summary: Using spectral imaging borrowed from a conservator friend, Ivo reads numbers painted into the frescoes' halos: dates, sums, initials. The ledger is a record of payments made to save the payers by naming the condemned. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: cold clarity—survival had a price list, and someone kept the receipts.

chapters.title: Reyes Closes In
chapters.summary: Reyes links the two deaths to San Remei survivors and suspects Ivo knows more than they say. Ivo gives her half-truths and watches her file them away like ammunition. POV: alternating Ivo and Reyes. Emotional beat: the loneliness of holding a truth that sounds like guilt.

chapters.title: The Third Letter
chapters.summary: No third death comes; instead a letter names the next target: Anselm. The handwriting, Ivo finally admits to themselves, is familiar—it belongs to someone from the archive's inner circle. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: panic giving way to a terrible shortlist of people Ivo loves.

chapters.title: San Remei
chapters.summary: Ivo travels to the ruined village and finds the memorial wall defaced: one name freshly repainted. A surviving neighbor, old Marta, recognizes Ivo and says, 'You came back to finish it?' POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: exile ending not with homecoming but with accusation.

chapters.title: Marta's Testimony
chapters.summary: Marta reveals that a boy from the village took the ledger when he fled, and that he swore to make the buyers pay when the statute neared expiry. She describes him without naming him—but Ivo knows the gait, the hands. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: dawning heartbreak as suspicion narrows to one beloved face.

chapters.title: Tomas
chapters.summary: Ivo confronts Tomás, the cathedral's gentle bookbinder and Ivo's closest friend, who neither denies nor confirms, only says: 'Read the last page before you judge me.' POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: loyalty cracking under the weight of evidence; love refusing to become certainty.

chapters.title: The Last Page
chapters.summary: Decoding the final fresco panel, Ivo finds the ledger's last entry: their own parents' names, sold by the men now dying—and a payment received by the person who raised Ivo afterward. The avenger's targets were the sellers; the murders are real, but so is the justice. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the ground shifting—grief, vindication, and horror braided together.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: With days left before the crimes legally expire, Ivo must decide: hand the decoded ledger to Reyes and bury Tomás, or stay silent and become what the killers became. Anselm urges silence; Reyes, unknowing, offers Ivo a way out. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh—loyalty versus truth, priced in full.

chapters.title: Anselm's Fall
chapters.summary: Before Ivo chooses, Anselm is attacked and left alive deliberately—a warning that the avenger knows Ivo has read the last page. In the hospital corridor, Anselm confesses his own small betrayals and absolves Ivo of nothing. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the collapse of every refuge; even sanctuary was rented.

chapters.title: Crypt Reckoning
chapters.summary: Ivo lures the avenger to the crypt with a forged letter and finds Tomás waiting beside the original ledger, hidden there since 1963. He confesses fully: the deaths, the letters, the years of watching Ivo grow into the person who might understand. POV: Ivo and Tomás. Emotional beat: climax—two survivors of the same crime facing each other across the only honest room in the city.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Tomás offers Ivo the ledger and his life: 'You're the archivist. Decide what history keeps.' Ivo calls Reyes. Tomás does not run. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the terrible peace of choosing truth over the last person who felt like family.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ivo surrenders the decoded ledger; the statute expires mid-investigation, but the fresco evidence unlocks cold-case prosecutions under newer laws. Reyes, respecting the cost, files her report with Ivo's cooperation noted but their name shielded. POV: Reyes, closing her case. Emotional beat: justice arriving sideways—imperfect, late, and real.

chapters.title: What the Archive Keeps
chapters.summary: Tomás, dying of illness accelerated by prison, asks Ivo to archive his testimony properly. Ivo catalogs it like any other document—complete, unflinching, signed by both of them. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into the only ritual Ivo trusts: preservation.

chapters.title: The Open Door
chapters.summary: A year later, the crypt is opened as a memorial; the frescoes are conserved with the ledger's story told plainly beside them. Ivo, no longer invisible, signs their full name to the exhibition plaque. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: resolution—survival's price paid at last, and worth it.
